question:
In the $\beta^-$-decay process
\[^{14}\!C\rightarrow ^{14}\!N + e^- + \bar\nu,\]
atomic masses are given as $M(^{14}\!C)=14.003242\,u$ and $M(^{14}\!N)=14.003074\,u$.</br>
Take $1\,u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$.</br>

(a) Using atomic masses, compute the $Q$-value of the decay.</br>
(b) If the neutrino carries negligible energy in a particular event and nuclear recoil is neglected, estimate the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron.</br>
(c) Evaluate the statement: “Because $Q$ is fixed, the emitted electron must have a fixed kinetic energy.”

options.A: $Q\approx 0.156\,\text{MeV}$, $K_{e,max}\approx 0.156\,\text{MeV}$, and the statement is incorrect due to energy sharing with the neutrino
options.B: $Q\approx 0.156\,\text{MeV}$, $K_{e,max}\approx 0.156\,\text{MeV}$, and the statement is correct because $Q$ is fixed
options.C: $Q\approx 1.56\,\text{MeV}$, $K_{e,max}\approx 1.56\,\text{MeV}$, and the statement is incorrect due to recoil only
